plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling rows of silvery-green shrubs erupt into waves of violet-blue flower spikes. The air hums with bees and carries a sweet, herbal perfume that drifts across the hills and farmland of Provence.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak bloom runs from mid-June to mid-July. Some areas keep flowering into August.
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its flowers produce an essential oil that has been used for centuries in perfumery, soaps and traditional remedies.

plants.name: Banksia menziesii
plants.description: A rugged Australian shrub with flower spikes like glowing cones. Hundreds of tiny golden and pink-red blooms are packed into each one. They glow in the winter bushland and feed honeyeaters and other nectar-loving wildlife.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn through early winter, roughly March to June, so it is still flowering around June 21, the Southern Hemisphere's winter solstice.
plants.funFact: The flower spikes open in a striking pattern, with the colors shifting from pink to gold as the tiny flowers open. The woody seed cones that follow open fully only after bushfire.
